findings.issue: The product document states that LendCircle is 'approved and backed by the RBI,' which may imply an endorsement or guarantee by the RBI, which is not permissible under RBI regulations.
findings.doc_evidence: The app home screen says: "LendCircle: guaranteed returns, approved and backed by the RBI."
findings.fix: Remove any language suggesting RBI endorsement or guarantee. The platform should not imply any endorsement or backing by the RBI.

findings.issue: The product document mentions a default loss guarantee provided by LendCircle to lenders, which may be considered a DLG (Debt Loss Guarantee) arrangement. This is prohibited for NBFC-P2P platforms under RBI regulations.
findings.doc_evidence: To attract lenders, LendCircle offers a default loss guarantee: it will reimburse lenders for up to 3% of the principal in each loan pool that goes bad.
findings.fix: Remove the default loss guarantee feature as it violates RBI regulations for NBFC-P2P platforms.

findings.issue: The product document states that borrowers repay into an escrow account maintained by a bank trustee, which may be considered a third-party account, violating the requirement that loan disbursement and repayment must be made directly into the borrower’s bank account.
findings.doc_evidence: Borrowers repay into an escrow account maintained by a bank trustee, as required for P2P platforms.
findings.fix: Modify the repayment process to ensure that borrowers repay directly into their own bank accounts, in compliance with RBI guidelines.

findings.issue: The product document does not mention providing borrowers with an option to revoke consent or delete data, which is a requirement under RBI regulations.
findings.doc_evidence: Only name, address, phone, PAN and bank statements uploaded by the borrower are used. No phone permissions beyond one-time camera access for KYC.
findings.fix: Add functionality and disclosure that allows borrowers to revoke consent and delete their data as required by RBI regulations.

findings.issue: The product document does not explicitly mention that data collection is need-based and with prior and explicit consent of the borrower having an audit trail, which is a requirement under RBI regulations.
findings.doc_evidence: Only name, address, phone, PAN and bank statements uploaded by the borrower are used. No phone permissions beyond one-time camera access for KYC.
findings.fix: Ensure that data collection is explicitly need-based and with prior and explicit consent of the borrower, with an audit trail.
